_about: The quick tour on each tool page: a click-through guide on the page itself (assets/js/guide.js). Each step highlights `s` (a CSS selector; a step whose element isn't on the page is skipped) with a title `t` and a tip `p`. `act` clicks something first (for example a tab); `restore` names what to click when the tour ends so the page is left as it was. Built into each tool page by build.py tour_link().

steps.p: It ranks the features you're weighing by what matters to your business, so your roadmap reflects your goals, not the loudest voice in the room.
Give it a name, so you can find it later.
Pick a template, then rename, reweight or add criteria. Effort and risk count the other way: lower is better.
Each slider sets a weight from 0 to 5. A weight of 0 switches a criterion off.
Score each feature from 1 to 5 on each criterion. Not sure where to start? Use Fill in an example to see how it works.
It updates as you go: a score from 0 to 100 for each feature, with what drove it.
Switch to RICE, add reach, impact, confidence and effort, and get a second ranking.
Puts the two rankings side by side. Where they disagree is where the real conversation is.
Save it to your account, share a link, or export a CSV or PDF. Nothing leaves your browser unless you choose to.
Have two people score on their own, then compare. For a whole team, save it to your account and choose Score as a team.
It helps you choose where AI is worth the effort first, and names the first pilot to run.
Name your list, so you can find it later.
Every idea is scored from 1 to 5 on business value, data readiness, cost and effort, team readiness, and risk if it goes wrong.
Add your ideas, one per row, as specific as you can. Use Fill in an example to see it work.
Value against feasibility. Quick wins sit top right; strategic bets are valuable but harder. A dashed ring flags high risk.
Every idea ranked with a next step. Start here names the first pilot: one team, four to six weeks, one number to judge it by.
Save it to your account, share a link, or export a CSV or PDF. Prefer a spreadsheet? There's an Excel version with the same math.
Score it with the people who'd use it, pilot one thing at a time, and re-run it after each pilot.
It checks whether your team, data, tools and guardrails are ready for AI work, and gives you your next three moves.
Name the check, for example by team and month.
24 statements in six areas, for your team as it is today: yes, partly, no or not sure. A no is more useful than a hopeful yes.
Your readiness score and what it means.
Your stage on the AI adoption journey, from starting with you to organization-wide capability, and a score for each area.
They come from the gaps in your weakest areas first, with what you said that led to each.
Save it, share a link, export it, or download the Excel version. Answer it together, act on one move at a time, and re-run it each quarter.

build-buy-partner.title: the Build, Buy, or Partner Matrix

steps.p: It helps you decide how to get a new capability (build it, buy it or partner for it) and record why.
Name the decision first.
Score each option from 1 to 5 on ten criteria, from strategic differentiation to exit flexibility. Weights add up to 100. Fill in the worked example to see it.
Compare the cost over three years. Years two and three often decide the outcome.
Each option's weighted score out of 5, its cost and its time to first value. Scores within a quarter point are a tie, which is common.
Where a small change in weights would change the answer, and the risks to plan for.
Why this option, the top risks, what would make you reopen it, and the next steps. It's saved with the matrix.
Save it, share a link, export it, or download the fillable PDF and spreadsheet versions.
It rates initiatives against the KPIs your organization already tracks, adjusts for how sure you are, and suggests what to do with each.
Name the sheet first.
Keep the defaults or rename them, and set their weights. Weights total 100.
Up to six initiatives: how much each would move each KPI (0 to 5), your confidence, and how easy it is to deliver. Fill in the worked example to see it.
The confidence-adjusted score against ease: do now, big bets, quick wins and revisit.
Every initiative in order, with a suggested action. Scores within five points are effectively tied.
Your top priority, sequencing, what you won't do now, and the assumptions to test first.
Save it, share a link, export it, or use the fillable PDF and spreadsheet versions.
